newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: G10 unhappy Padoa-Schioppa leaving Basle committee.
newsitem.headline: G10 unhappy Padoa-Schioppa leaving Basle committee.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said the G10 was not happy about the departure of Tommaso Padoa-Schioppa as chairman of the Basle Committee on Banking Supervision "because he did a very good job".
To the lament of central bankers, Italy's cabinet last month nominated Padoa-Schioppa, chairman of the Basle Committee since 1993, to head that country's stock market regulator Consob.
Tietmeyer said this means Padoa-Schioppa would resign as committee chairman.

"Of course we are not happy about that because he did a very good job," Tietmeyer told reporters after the monthly meeting of G10 central bankers, adding the G10 would decide on a new chairman in the near future.
The issue of banking supervision was discussed extensively by G10 governors, with the topic focused on whether more regulation is better than less, he said.
Teitmeyer said the governors did not reach any conclusions on this issue and would await the findings of three Basle Committee sub-groups grappling with these questions.
Another topic discussed was the protection of investor deposits and the maintenance of systemic stability in financial markets. This raised the question of the importance of disclosure standards.
"There is agreement disclosure is a very important instrument, but of course it has its limits," Tietmeyer said.

The third topic discussed was capital standards and whether this was still an appropriate approach. In 1988 the Basle Committee issued its guidelines for international banks to have capital of at least eight percent of risk-weighted assets.
He added that more recently the committee had amended the Capital Accord to capture market risks as well, a move Tietmeyer described as an "important improvement".
"The question is whether this is already the end of the road or whether we can go further," Tietmeyer added.
